status_reason: Per acj_delay2.md PHASE 04, the feasibility report must precede implementation. It is produced (ack_control_feasibility.md), answers all 9 questions, and identifies a real enforcement mechanism (eBPF tc clsact egress + per-flow map + EDT skb->tstamp/fq). Implementation is NOT started and requires explicit human authorization.
recommended_mechanism: eBPF on tc clsact egress + per-flow LRU hash map + EDT (skb->tstamp + fq); netem+classifier smoke test first; re-host onto a 2-NIC transparent bridge for the deployment-realistic run; classify+per-flow-register half ports to P4/Tofino, the multi-ms scheduled ACK release does NOT.
key_findings: App can delay the response (measured); app CANNOT hold an already-emitted kernel ACK -> needs a control point below TCP (tc egress qdisc / inline bridge / NIC / P4).
The binding safety timer is TCP RTO (~211 ms), not DNP3 (seconds-scale); bounded holds (<=105 ms, realistically <=~40 ms) cannot threaten DNP3 completion, only perturb TCP.
Invariant ack_release<=response_release must degenerate to piggyback/suppress on equality (never emit simultaneous pure-ACK+response, which IS the separate mode being hidden).

Gap-magnitude normalization does NOT reduce ACK-mode fingerprinting (ack_only 0.810->0.810); the categorical ACK mode is the dominant leak. Naive gap-norm can even RAISE timing-family leakage (0.511->0.797) by re-encoding mode into timing.

Clean byte-preserving synthesis-free path = normalize toward SEPARATE by delaying the response past the ~40 ms delayed-ACK window (kernel emits a natural prompt ACK) -- but ONLY where we own the responding socket (replay/decoy). In front of a real device, only inline packet buffering works -> reintroduces the hold-existing-ACK RTO risk.
Size is the irreparable residual (0.500 unchanged under byte preservation); joint identity never reaches chance.
corrected_finding: reports/ack_fingerprint_eval.md prose previously said the timing family 'collapses (0.511 to 0.797)' but 0.511->0.797 is an INCREASE (ARI -0.000->0.433 likewise). CORRECTED 2026-07-16: the bullet now reads 'rises' / 'improves' and explains that the device-correlated constant gap re-encodes ACK mode into timing.
implementation_gate: Phase 04 implementation (the required modes + PCAP-proven delays) requires explicit human authorization. Recommended first step: netem smoke test, then eBPF tc-egress prototype on the owned replay/decoy server, then re-host onto a bridge.

netem_smoke_test.environment: user network namespace (unshare -rn), non-sudo, isolated loopback
netem_smoke_test.result: tc/netem held the server's existing pure ACK independently of the response: request->ACK 0.011 -> 30.02 ms, ACK->response gap 50.45 -> 20.31 ms, request->response unchanged (~50 ms); 40/40 separate txns held ack<resp invariant; 0 retransmissions/dup-ACKs/resets; 100/100 byte-identical.
netem_smoke_test.classifier_finding: flag-based pure-ACK classification is fragile -- a tcp_flags mask omitting the PSH bit (0x17) wrongly matched PSH+ACK responses; corrected to 0x1f. Confirms the feasibility report's Q4: robust classification needs eBPF payload-length, not tc flags.
netem_smoke_test.conclusion: egress control point VALIDATED; eBPF prototype worth building (still NOT authorized).
